finding.title: Concurrent reader sees mixed output generations during an otherwise successful refresh
finding.distinction: Prior A output-generation fault injection required a failed second/third write; this test pauses a successful writer after its first write and proves the transient mixed snapshot is externally readable without any write exception.
finding.source_mechanism: storage.atomic_write_json atomically replaces each single file; runner.run_once writes latest.json, audit_latest.json, anata_latest.json sequentially with no common publication commit marker or cross-file read barrier.

isolated_test.fixture: Three G0 JSON files; background writer calls copied storage.atomic_write_json for G1 latest, blocks at Event; reader opens all three files; writer then completes remaining G1 writes.
assertions: After writer completes without exception all three are [G1,G1,G1].

exact_repo_oracle.setup: At pinned SHA use real runner.run_once(network=False,external_jsonl=[G1],local_dir=tmp_path,as_of_ms=T1) after G0 baseline. Monkeypatch runner.atomic_write_json with a deterministic barrier after first file replacement; concurrent reader opens latest.json,audit_latest.json,anata_latest.json while writer is paused.
exact_repo_oracle.expected_failure: A single reader snapshot must not mix generations or must explicitly detect/retry an incomplete generation; current sequential publication permits G1 latest with G0 audit/handoff.
extra_assertions: Writer completes successfully and all three files then reflect G1.
Archive admission and retry remain idempotent and order-independent after partial-batch failure.
Audit, handoff and evidence_health PIT fields reflect a single as_of and provenance generation.

finding.proof_limits: The isolated test reproduces publication ordering with a verbatim function copy; no exact-repository pytest, no actual consumer race or production incident demonstrated.
